paper.citation: Dimitriadis, T., Dümbgen, L., Henzi, A., Puke, M. and Ziegel, J. (2023). Honest calibration assessment for binary outcome predictions. Biometrika, 110(3), 663-680. DOI: 10.1093/biomet/asac068.
paper.venue: Biometrika (formal publication, 2023); arXiv preprint v2 is the checked DGP version
paper.source_locator: DGP source actually checked in arXiv:2203.04065v2 (2022-11-02), PDF p.8, Section 5, item 4 (Step): upper staircase p_s(x)=(floor(k*x)+1{x!=1})/k with k=15-10*s; X~U[0,1] and Y~Bernoulli{p_s(X)} are specified on the same page. Supplementary Material PDF pp.17-20 covers rounding, application details and proofs and does not state a changed step DGP. The paper gives replication URL https://github.com/marius-cp/replication_DDHPZ22 but no fixed code commit. Formal Biometrika DGP differences were not checked [*].

mechanism.name: Upper step binary regression functions from Dimitriadis et al. (2023)

sampling.dependence: iid across observations; no cluster, panel, network, or within-unit dependence

assumptions: Independent and identically distributed individual observations (X_i,Y_i).
X has the source distribution Uniform[0,1] and the fixed query x*=0.5 lies in its support interior.
Given X=x, Y is Bernoulli with success probability p_s(x)=(floor(k*x)+1{x!=1})/k; k=15-10*s is a positive integer in {5,...,14} for the declared scenarios.

For every declared scenario s in {0.1,...,1.0}, p_s is nondecreasing and right-continuous on [0,1] with p_s(0)=1/k>0 and p_s(1)=1, satisfying the monotonicity condition used for the source simultaneous-band method.
The scalar truth is evaluated under the known DGP; no causal exchangeability, treatment, mediator, or interference assumption is relevant.

properties.notes: The only covariate is X, so total and effective dimensions are both one. There are no interaction terms. The regression function is a piecewise-constant (step) function with k equal-height jumps at x=0,1/k,2/k,...,(k-1)/k; this is nonlinear (non-smooth). The binary outcome link is Bernoulli with this conditional probability. The function is discontinuous at each knot x=j/k (right-continuous from the left: value jumps up at the knot). The s=0 endpoint is excluded because k=15 is outside the declared range {5,...,14}.

estimand.name: m_s(x*) = E[Y | X=x*] = p_s(x*)
estimand.definition: Noncausal nonparametric regression function at the fixed query x*=0.5 for a selected source scenario s in {0.1,0.2,...,1.0}; the step function is p_s(x)=(floor(k*x)+1{x!=1})/k with k=15-10*s, yielding a piecewise-constant right-continuous function with k equal steps of height 1/k. The target is a conditional Bernoulli probability, not an intervention effect or a prediction interval.

truth.derivation: Exact step formula: p_s(0.5)=(floor(k*0.5)+1)/k, k=15-10*s; this is exact rational arithmetic. For default s=0.5 (k=10): floor(5.0)=5, p=(5+1)/10=6/10=0.6. Independently verified with fractions.Fraction exact rational arithmetic in verify.py.

adaptations: Register s=0.1,0.2,...,1.0 as named scenarios (s=0 excluded per the source upper-step definition k=15-10*s in {5,...,14}); these are source parameter settings, not new mechanism families.
Expose the scalar NRI target p_s(0.5)=E[Y|X=0.5] required by the collection interface. The source studies simultaneous confidence bands under monotonicity, not this scalar truth hook.
Run the collection smoke check instead of the source's 1000-replication coverage experiment; no confidence band, bootstrap, or coverage result is claimed.
